reviews.text: I put in a lot of hours into the demo, wishlisted this and was looking forward to the official release. It's barely a complete game. You'll randomly scroll through different in game menus and see ERROR CHAMPION DESCRIPTION 404 NOT AVAILABLE text on items. You gather keys during the stages and when you complete the run you don't even get to keep them, like the mechanic doesn't even work and that's how you would upgrade your maps. Speaking of maps you can't even access the third one currently due to the aforementioned error message. Some of the enemies names are one thing, but the character models don't match the name. It feels like an early access title that was rushed to full production and then slapped with a price tag in a hurry. I wonder if some of these devs even play their own games sometimes to catch all of the simple errors or if we're just rushing releases in order to get paid. I wouldn't recommend this game in it's current state, just play the free demo until they get around to fixing everything. Core concept and merges are fun, needs about triple the content and characters in order to be worth the price tag.
Do not buy in the current state, unfinished, meta currency not working, lags and bugs. edit: even after the "fixes" it still lags and there's still placeholder text around

玩法就跟War3某平台的一些图一样，简单总结就是单人循环圈+元素TD的合成塔玩法。 但目前有问题，局内打的钥匙无法结算，解锁的图鉴也无法保存，等于说没有存档功能。（公告说是修复了，但我这里还是这问题） 价位也不贵，目前差评都是针对这个问题而不是游戏本身的质量。 相比国内某平台上同样玩法的地图动不动来什么“宝箱抽取”“付费月卡”“收费道具”做的还不好玩的烂图。 这个很值得一玩。 抛开存档问题，机翻也挺乐呵的，也不知道是英译中还是韩译中，湿婆翻译成了屎……某种程度还挺对的，毕竟是印度神仙嘛。 翻译问题虽多但不影响游玩，没有“老头滚动条”“踢牙老奶奶”这种完全无法理解的，技能效果，装备效果，虽然是机翻但还是能看懂。 就看后续还有没有更新了，毕竟不是作为EA测放上来而是作为“正式版”放出来的，希望后续能更新更多内容吧。

Genuinely, this game was really fun right when it released. However, every single patch (and there are multiple per day at this point) seems geared toward making the game harder and harder, and I literally cannot understand the reason for that. It's a single player game. There are no leaderboards. I had the most fun when this game felt casual and gave me the nostalgic joy of old Warcraft III custom maps. Now... well, now it feels like fighting for my life even on some of the lower difficulties, and it takes all of the fun out of the "combine dudes to make bigger dudes" search because you're just making whatever you can throw together to survive. I have no idea why the devs decided that this game needs to be hard, but it feels antithetical to the core mechanics of fusing things together to make cooler stuff if you have to prioritize strategy over searching for things to fuse into cooler things.

I played it to completion, it's somewhat interesting, but it ultimately feels like a student project. Sadly I'm not sure if it will go anywhere unless the whole hero upgrade system is overhauled, really not fond of losing out on unique abilities of a given lower-tiered hero for a completely different one upon merging. despite decent variety of heroes, it all feels flat since I would just get merged all the way to transcendent heroes and automatically win, even on Torment 5 difficulty. Overall, I saw the dev's roadmap and it boils down to adding leaderboards and more heroes, and I don't think just adding more heroes is good enough to justify this game's price point. In my humble opinion, the game in its current state and developmental approach, values less than the price it's being sold for.

I really liked the concept. The heroes are stylish and fun and I loved that I could get Napoleon commanding my troops. However after a little while it became a math simulator. I'd have screenshots of what I'd need to build for the next troop in the tree. There was no way to automate that in the game or set a "build path" really could use that quality of life change, may have kept playing but as it stands I don't want a spreadsheet emulator with a nice GUI.

Skill expression is minimal. Torment is just boring because it is a 10 minute long wait timer on if I get to play the run or not. Shop needs a rework. Players should have more ability to chase with intent instead of just hoping that the gamble works out. As is, don't purchase.

Fun for a short period, but (at least as of now) it's lacking any replayability. Things that might help: - Achievements/leaderboards (I know this is on the roadmap) - some reason to want to play again and again - More impactful "prestige" rewards - More impactful differences between units/unit-types. My current "strategy" is to keep combining units to get to transcendent as fast as possible, but I haven't had a need on, say, a specific map type to beeline or focus for a specific hero. (ex. Str vs Dex vs Int based) Putting a heavier emphasis on mob "types" spawning on an entire map (ex. magic vs phys resistant; small swarms vs big single-targets) would help make unit build paths more meaningful

For the price this is a good game, I know work on it is continuing with a road map but there are a few things I'd recommend people know ahead of time. Visual clutter gets pretty intense, you'll want to turn options lower, cap your framerate, and also turn off dmg numbers and attack effects - late game gets pretty intensive. It's a fun game but doesn't have a tremendous amount of depth, pretty much everything is available to you out the get go and the only real difference in maps are difficulty modifiers. Torment difficulty is interesting, but after you get the meager selection of upgrades your keys just become a currency to use at the Black Market which isn't usually worth it unless you want to spend them later in the run because you're going for a long endless attempt. You'll find that the critical level up options are interesting at first but you'll really only settle on one or two you like, the others probably won't be impactful enough to even tempt you to try them. Now for things I'd like to see from the game. I know that there is a balance in how many characters you can have total, otherwise it'd become difficult/impossible to map out or plan on which heroes to move towards, but I think that with how many "Statues" that give you a direct line to picking which heroes you want, I'd like to see more options and upgrade paths. More meta-upgrades. A little bit of starting stats and a tiny % of additional keys are okay as a base, but to allow additional upgrade paths to incentivize the level-up rewards would be really cool to see. Better balance on top-end heroes, there are a couple I really prioritize which causes the game to feel same-y outside of the early game which becomes trying to figure out *how* to get to that one Transcendent hero. Overall I'd love to see more options and wider ranges for upgrades, heroes, etc. But again for the price this is a good, fun, bite sized game!
